1.name: Potential
1.fn: Supply. An internal supply. It completes into the River at 4.
1.img: Hidden power, the unknown and unmanifested. Potential in the electrical sense too: voltage held, nothing yet flowing. The High Priestess is the water itself, the scroll half hidden, the law under the surface.
1.shadow: Timid Boy (the fear state; over-engineering is what he does with it, building the apparatus so he never has to step) ↔ Blue Belt (rash: has been under before and come up with something, and mistakes that for knowing the depths; earned the right to be confident, not the right to be sure). Balanced: Courage, facing fear with preparation. The axis reads timid, blue belt, courage.
1.practice: Deep meditation is warranted on water days. The fork at the water is mystery or fear, and that fork is healthy, not shadow.
1.tarot: The Fool, stepping off into the Priestess's water.
1.rejected: Names: the well, then the depths. Over-Engineer and Unmoored, kept as the mechanisms under the two figures. Drowner, Plunger, Deep End, Compulsive. For the Balanced: Black Belt, Diver, Initiate, Swimmer, Apprentice, Precocious Child, Hero. For the name: Wuji, Pleroma, Tehom, Source, Abyss, Seed, Reservoir, among others.

2.name: Field
2.img: The field is the capacity to receive, not the crop. Three open lines, nothing concealed. It says yes to everything.
2.shadow: Smotherer (Jung's devouring mother: over-cultivation, can't stop tending, digs the seed up) ↔ Stagnation (the abandoning mother: she has left the field to rot; Erikson's stagnation, whose two failures, overextension and rejectivity, are this axis). Balanced: Generative, which is wu wei. The Empress at her best does nothing and everything grows; only the Balanced field produces.
2.practice: Say yes. Don't dig the seed up to check on it; the work is being done underneath. 2 is germinating, not eroding: live the 2 day with the end in mind. Haner: Germination, the year of planting seeds; keywords Stagnation, Preparation, Listening, Friendship.
2.tarot: The Empress, the generative mother. The Gnostic 2 is The Magnetic, The Bearer: the mare bears its load, and the editor quotes Case on Daleth, the Empress's own letter.
2.rejected: Hoarfrost (replaced 28 Oct: the field is not frozen, it is left to rot). Calm (the abandoning mother looks calm from outside). Hoarder, Spendthrift, Scorched, Ghost, Deserter, Locust, Blight, Fallow, Warden. For the Balanced: Bearing, Patience, Devotion, Presence, Trust, Ripening.
2.fam: mother · southwest · late summer, fertile or scorched ground
2.chat: Shadow side of two and eight · this chat, 28 Oct

3.name: Power
3.fn: The first of the three forces. One third in, from outside; it happens to you. A given loan of energy, not income, spent on one job: reach the light. Strong force in a weak body; fast, vulnerable, forward.
3.img: 51 Shock. Force from the outside in. Thunder cracking the surface.
3.shadow: Manic Wildfire (thunder on the untended field: Stagnation at 2 leaves dry material, and the energy is spent overcorrecting for the neglect; it takes everything at once and topples) ↔ Argos (Greek argós, "without work": the charge that never fires; meets the mentor and goes home; the shock comes anyway, harder; Odysseus's dog on the dung heap, the hundred-eyed watcher). Balanced: Composure. Shadows at the triangle are conditions, not figures. The passive of 2 becoming the active of 3 may be a rule: the Triforce flips polarity.
3.practice: Spend exactly enough to break the surface. Adjust tempo, keep the goal, double-check premises. The source of this strike is the previous octave's 9.
3.tarot: The Ace of Wands: the hand from the cloud holding a sprouting wand, the loan handed in from outside, the leaves already falling as it is spent. And the Emperor: Aries, the first fire of spring, power as authority. The Knight of Wands is the Wildfire, not the point.
3.rejected: Thunder as the headline (28 Oct). Shock as the headline. Convert, Bunker, Flash Flood, Early Bloom, Bolting, Mayfly, Heir, Golden Boy. For tarot: the Tower, Judgement, Wheel of Fortune.
3.fam: eldest son · east · spring, the cotyledon bursting through soil
3.chat: Reflecting on the system's past days

4.name: River
4.fn: Supply and cultivate running together: the River. On the hexad it traces to 2; the Delta is downstream on the path of time, not on the hexad.
4.img: Rooted wood, flexible above because the roots are deep and fed by water. Healthy four is rooted.
4.shadow: Paralyzer (stands in the doorway doubting; no root to stand on) ↔ Drifter (goes wherever the wind already blows; motion without a choice). Maturation: Timid Boy → Paralyzer, Blue Belt → Drifter (his confidence was never a real choice, so by 4 it is momentum, and momentum is the wind). Boy forms at 1, man forms at 4, the same line as 5 → 7.
4.practice: The Magician is the four day reading the one day's note. The piece of scroll is on the table; point it one way.
4.tarot: The Magician choosing the wand: the Fool numbered, the same substance in its next state.

5.name: Delta
5.fn: No fixed function. A point of karma: the place where time loops from a larger cycle down into a smaller one. It inherits the larger picture's perspective. A port of time; a place to rest and reflect on what the larger cycle brought, perhaps at the end of the day. The classical center: everything comes to you and nothing is displaced; stay put, receive, do not initiate.
5.img: Your image: the yin-yang holding still, opposites holding each other's seeds. Receives both 8's one held thing and the larger picture.
5.shadow: High Chair Tyrant ↔ Weakling Prince. Balanced: the Divine Child, the boy form of the King (Moore & Gillette). "Works for now; may rename later."
5.practice: Unblock, whatever that means in the moment: mental, emotional, physical. Tend to yourself, not outward, so that what is coming through can land. Clear the channel, so the reflection at 7 is true and the cut at 6 rings clear.
5.tarot: Three cards, read together, because three things land at once: the order from above (the Hierophant, who receives it and gives it), the turn of the larger cycle (the Wheel of Fortune), and the karmic bind (the Devil, Capricorn: "if 5 is about karma, what better judge than Capricorn, Saturn and time itself"). The Lo Shu is Saturn's own square, with 5 at its center.
5.since: 23–25 Oct, done for now; named 28 Oct
5.fam: the center · inherits the nearest higher cycle that is not 5 (day from month, month from year)
5.chat: Passive poll five · this chat, 30 Oct

6.name: Will
6.fn: The second force, the one circumstance cannot supply. Two thirds in; from the inside out. Sustained will against dispersal: drift, inner entropy. Not a fight with the ego (the ego is the warrior) and not with imbalance (the symptom). The dragon is internal at 6; unconquered, it sits down and hoards at 8.
6.img: 1 The Dynamic. Force from the inside out, brought under will. The sickle separating wheat from chaff.
6.shadow: Self-Righteousness (the ego's will passed off as the Self's; acts as if right no matter what; cuts what doesn't need cutting) ↔ Indulgence (the ego's appetite with the Self forgotten; gives in and forgets there was anything right to do). Balanced: Divine Will, adherence to the higher Self.
6.q: What was the ego magnetic to?
6.practice: Doing the right thing and sticking to it when nothing pushes you. First half readiness, second half action. Integrity is the result of an integrated 6. Whether the strike was made decides whether the next octave is a loop or a spiral.
6.tarot: Strength: the hand closing the lion's mouth, the life force held under will, gently and tirelessly. And Justice: the sword is the sickle, the scales weigh what to carry, Libra begins at the autumn equinox when the harvest is in and the cutting back starts; her keyword is integrity, and her shadow is the judge who is sure and wrong.
6.rejected: Discernment (placeholder, 28–29 Oct). Heaven. Courage, because it collides with 1's Balanced. Arrogant Dragon, Passenger, Zealot, Prodigal, Reaper. For tarot: the Lovers (choice between attractions, not discernment), the Emperor (taken by 3).
6.chat: Reflecting on the system's past days

7.name: Lake
7.fn: Reflection, the settling. What landed at 5 becomes clear because a lake is reflective. In the nine-year mapping: force and cultivate, the Mountain standing up to take the yield.
7.img: The King in his triumph: sees the reflection, leaves it still, and acts from it right away. The reflection informs him; it does not belong to him. The lake's virtue is emptiness; it fails when overfull or disturbed.
7.shadow: Tyrant (grasps the reflection to control it, which breaks the picture: hasty decisions, ruin, loses the loyalty of his forces) ↔ Princess (Haner's image: smooths the surface over despite knowing what is beneath; control by doing nothing). Balanced: the King.
7.practice: Stop, look at what is already there, say what is plain, do that one thing. Write the sentence.
7.tarot: The Chariot: 7 in motion from stillness. Waite: the Chariot is the King in his triumph, the victory that creates kingship.
7.rejected: Reveler, Smoother, Grasper. The imagery (the lake filling, the king leaving the shore) was flagged as shaky on 25 Oct and settled on 30 Oct: the lake reflects 5 directly.
7.fam: youngest daughter · west · autumn, harvest and celebration
7.chat: Passive poll five · Reflecting on the system's past days

8.name: Mountain
8.fn: Cultivate and boundary: the Mountain, still. The first pattern on the hexad to cross Gardener and Warrior. The boundary is passive, a wall that stands; a cultivated boundary grew, it was not built. The Hermit's boundary is the lantern, not a fence.
8.img: The one thing that lasted, held visible, not planted. Keeping is not hiding; it is not touching. Haner: the Transformer; the 8 year is the caterpillar in the cocoon; in the mountain there is a cave, and the cave holds the treasure.
8.shadow: Dragon, the Hoarder (over-closing: lives in the mountain but is not the mountain; keeps instead of carries; the Warrior half taking over; an unconquered dragon at 6 sits down here) ↔ Barrow, the Recluse (the grave, the mound of the dead: keeps nothing; the Gardener half failing). Balanced: Stillness. Maturation: Smotherer → Dragon, Stagnation → Barrow. Quality of an 8 day: choose one mountain; 52, keeping the back still.
8.q: This is what lasted. Not touching it yet.
8.practice: Keep the one thing that lasted and hold it still. It feels like wrapping up the whole cycle.
8.tarot: The Hermit, old on the card because he has carried what the mother made the longest.
8.fam: youngest son · northeast · the hour before dawn, the dormant seed
8.chat: Shadow side of two and eight · Reflecting on the system's past days

9.name: Clarity
9.fn: The third force: source and arrival, the seeing from which the strikes come and to which they return. 9 sees rather than stages. In the nine-year mapping, the Ocean: collects everything, keeps nothing; the King; no function; pure sight.
9.img: 30 Clarity. The force that sees the two as one. Light that lives on what it burns.
9.shadow: Settled for now without named poles; the failure is sleep. Pontificator / Sleeper were offered and not taken.
9.practice: See one clear question; do not act on it directly. Its clarity is itself activating and can spread you thin. Its clarity is the source of the next octave's 3 and 6.
9.tarot: The Sun and the World, for now. The Sun: the child on the white horse, nothing hidden, nothing carried; 9 as what it does, the seeing. The World: the dancer in the wreath, completion that is also the start, the wreath a zero; 9 as where it sits, source and arrival.
9.since: origin notes, 9 Oct; settled for now 30 Oct
9.chat: Reflecting on the system's past days

Wood.Wood: The forest. Growth crowds growth. Choose one trunk and prune the rest.

Fire.Earth: Fire becoming ash. You give yourself to the field. An ending that fertilizes.
Fire.Metal: The forge. You shape the field; you are the smith. Patience with the heat.

Earth.Wood: Roots in the soil. The field draws on you. Yield; do not resist what is growing.
Earth.Fire: Ash enriching the ground. The field feeds you. A carried time; receive it.
Earth.Earth: Earth on earth. Weight and stillness. Nothing cuts, nothing pushes; the risk is Stagnation. Do not grasp.
Earth.Metal: Earth bearing ore. You give the field its form. It costs, and something is made.

Metal.Water: Metal yielding water. You are drained into flow. Let go; you are turning into motion.
Metal.Wood: The blade. You cut the field. Discernment: cut only what needs cutting.
Metal.Fire: In the forge. You are being reshaped by heat you did not choose. Hold form; submit to the work.
Metal.Earth: Ore in the mountain. The field holds and forms you. Rest in it.
Metal.Metal: Metal on metal. Sharpness doubled. Clarity or brittleness; do not over-cut.

1.line: Winter. Dormancy and the hidden work; rest, plan, do not push.

2.line: Germination. Preparation, listening, slow groundwork; the risk is Stagnation.

3.line: Spring. Sudden starts and new energy that outruns its body; begin, but keep Composure.

4.line: Growth. Expansion, travel, communication; things take off and can scatter.

5.line: The pivot. Everything comes to you and nothing is displaced; stay put, receive, do not initiate.

6.line: Authority. Responsibility and the first harvest; maturity with a perfectionist edge.

7.line: Harvest. Joy, money, reflection, pleasure and its excesses.

8.line: The turning point. Stillness before change; revolution held in the mountain.

9.line: Illumination. Recognition and exposure; things come to light.

1>4.lines: Nourish. Top line only, yin → yang. Kan becomes Xun. The water stays under as root and the firm thing rises. Water generates Wood.
1>4.shadows: Timid Boy = no line moves (Kan stays Kan, nothing surfaced) → Paralyzer at 4. Blue Belt = too many lines move (Li or Qian, all surface, no root) → Drifter at 4. The Balanced is exactly one line moving, the right one.
1>4.hex: 59 Dispersion (Xun over Kan): the wind moves what the water held, outward, across the great water. 48 The Well (Kan over Xun): the bucket going down; too short a rope is the Timid Boy, a broken jug the Blue Belt.
1>4.tarot: The Fool goes into the Priestess's water and comes back up as the Magician. Same person at two different times.
1>4.practice: What the one day went under for, the four day points one way.

4>2.note: Drafted 23 Oct, locked 30 Oct. "Magnetic and dynamic", not regressive.
4>2.lines: Break. Lines 3 and 6 both go yang → yin. Xun becomes Kun. Wood breaks Earth: the plow, the one link on the controlling cycle and the single half-step on the circuit.
4>2.shadows: Failure modes: Smotherer / Stagnation. Undershoot: Xun stays (Drifter). Top line only turns → Kan, a regress to 1. Middle line only → Gen, the field sealed unworked.
4>2.hex: 46 Pushing Upward (Kun over Xun), locked 30 Oct: a turn toward the Self (south is 9, between southeast and southwest on the Lo Shu); the pace of a tree; the Magician grows what will fall. 20 Contemplation is background only.
4>2.tarot: The Magician's wand going into the Empress's earth.
4>2.practice: The direction stops being something you steer and becomes something you give to the ground.
4>2.chat: Octave Method: 7-1-4 · Reflecting on the system's past days

2>8.lines: Inherit. Line 6 firms. Kun becomes Gen. Earth to Earth, no element change: one element in two states. The trace runs through the Lo Shu center, so it reads as inheritance, not movement. 8's one yang line is boundary, not force.
2>8.shadows: Undershoot: Kun stays Kun, the field left to rot, nothing grows a skin and there is nothing for 8 to hold (Stagnation → Barrow). Overshoot: the top line firms too early, Gen before the field has been received (the Smotherer → Dragon).
2>8.hex: 23 Disintegration (Gen over Kun), confirmed 30 Oct as the one figure for the line: do not act, meaning don't grasp; the superior man stabilizes his responses; line 6 the large fruit still uneaten, the carriage; the Hermit inherits only the one fruit. 15 Temperance (Kun over Gen) is held loosely as the inversion: the mountain hidden beneath the earth, greatness held underneath.
2>8.tarot: Empress → Hermit. 15 is the Hermit already standing in the Empress's garden, hidden by the bloom; 23 is the Hermit alone on the stripped ground.
2>8.practice: 2 says yes to everything; 8 keeps the one thing that lasted and holds it still, visible, not planted.
2>8.chat: Octave Method: 2-8-5 · Okta strategy and Enneagram pairs · Shadow side of two and eight

8>5.note: Settled 30 Oct; no fixed hexagram, since 5 has no trigram.
8>5.lines: Keep. 5 has no trigram; it borrows the larger cycle's. The hexagram is built on the day: the inherited trigram over Gen. The moving lines measure the distance between what was kept at 8 and what the larger cycle demands, and the Gnostic line texts are the prescription.
8>5.shadows: If 8 isn't lived, 5 balances you from outside: karmic retribution.
8>5.hex: Built on the day, inherited trigram over Gen. In a Kan month: 39. In a Kun month: 15. The 23 Oct worked example (Gen → Kan, 39, lines 5 and 6) was this rule before it was stated.
8>5.practice: 5 is the one place the day touches the larger cycle; 8 is the virtue that opens it. The one held thing carried into the Delta together with the larger picture.
8>5.chat: Okta strategy and Enneagram pairs · Reflecting on the system's past days

5>7.note: Settled 30 Oct; hexagram rule stated the same day. 7's imagery no longer shaky. Mapping all nine changing lines for 5 deferred.
5>7.lines: Reflect. Earth generates Metal. The hexagram is built on the day: Dui over the inherited trigram. The lake reflects whatever 5 inherited.
5>7.shadows: High Chair Tyrant / Weakling Prince at 5 mature into Tyrant / Princess at 7.
5>7.hex: Built on the day, Dui over the inherited trigram. In a Kan month: 60. In a Kun month: 45.
5>7.tarot: Hierophant → Chariot: the order received from above, then that order in motion.
5>7.practice: 5 hands what it received to the lake. 7 sees the reflection, leaves it still, acts from it right away.
5>7.chat: Passive poll five · Inner circuitry study progress · Reflecting on the system's past days

7>1.note: Worked 26 Oct. A trace is both contained within its own octave and extends into the next; this is an octave trace.
7>1.lines: Shape. Only line 1 changes, yang → yin: the lake floor opens. Dui becomes Kan. Metal generates Water, the one octave trace that runs with the generative cycle.
7>1.shadows: Lines carry no shadows of their own (30 Oct). Two failure modes: the lake held full, nothing goes under; the lake run out over the field, nothing channeled.
7>1.hex: 47 Oppression (Kan over Dui): the dry lake bed; the water is below, out of reach from the surface; the superior man stakes everything on will; sacrifice with sincerity. 48 The Well is 47 rotated: the same water, seen from where one draws it. 60 Limitation (Dui over Kan), the inversion, held loosely: a light heart over the source.
7>1.tarot: The Chariot left on the shore; the King gets down and stands at the edge as the Fool (26 Oct reading).
7>1.practice: In practice it is a seed: 7 writes the sentence, acts once, closes the entry and does not reread it; 1 reads it.

paras: The hexad carries residue, never a verdict. Each line hands forward what its origin could not finish: 1 leaves what the water held for 4, 2 leaves the one surviving thing for 8, 5 leaves what landed for 7 to reflect. That is stigmergy: an agent responding to a trace, with no plan above it. It is why the circuit is perfectly efficient and why it cannot lift itself.

A human is not a termite. We leave psychological traces as well as physical ones. When the trace written at a point is a story about the point ("this happened because I am inadequate") instead of what was observed there, the line carries the story forward as if it were residue. 4 then grows the story 1 told, 8 keeps the story 2 told, 7 reflects the story 5 told. The spiral still turns, the hexad still feeds, and every pass confirms the narrative. This is a loop at the same level, not an octave. In the essay's terms, a termite will build a mound over a piece of trash if it carries the right scent.

The Triforce is the only remedy, because the hexad has no force of its own. 6 is the veto: the conscious decision not to build on a poisoned trace. 3 is the shock from outside that breaks the ground the story was growing in. 9 is the sight that recognizes the trace as a story at all. None of these can arrive from inside the hexad. A spiral that bends downward is one where the shocks were not made and the stories were carried. A spiral that rises is one where the trace stayed residue and the shocks were received at 3, made at 6, and seen at 9.

Practice: the trace written at Reflect is an observation, never a verdict. "I was avoidant" is itself a trace. Note where the energy went, note which story showed up, and leave judgement to the pattern across many days.

items: 3 Power: the first force, one third in, from outside. A given loan of energy, not income. Gardener. Balanced: Composure.

6 Will: the second force, two thirds in, from the inside out. The one thing circumstance cannot supply and the hexad cannot generate. Warrior. Balanced: Divine Will. Whether the strike was made decides loop or spiral.
9 Clarity: the third force, source and arrival, the reconciling: the seeing from which the strikes come and to which they return. 9 sees rather than stages.
"Given shock" and "made shock" are retired from the lexicon; they stay only as Gurdjieff's source in the reasoning.

Triangle points carry active and passive shadows like the hexad, but as conditions, not figures. The passive of 2 becoming the active of 3 (Stagnation → Manic Wildfire) may be a rule: the Triforce flips polarity.
Forces are qualities and rotate; points are positions. Not a duality, a trinity: the Earth turning produces the pair; dawn and dusk are where the third force shows.
The three Lo Shu families sum to 3, 6, 9 mod 9. The Law of Three is in the hexad's own material.
Families: 1·4·7 receptive (Kan, Xun, Dui); 2·5·8 substrate (Kun, center, Gen); 3·6·9 expansive (Zhen, Qian, Li). Add 3 and you stay in your family at any size of square.

2-5-8 is the only diagonal that is itself a family and it is the mirror axis: reflect across it and the yin family lands on the yang family (1↔3, 4↔6, 7↔9). On the infinite tiling the three families are three parallel diagonal lines.
The Lo Shu is a yin-yang symbol as numbers: 9 and 1 are each other's seed; Kan and Li straddle the line, each carrying its opposite inside.
Seasons: 1 deep winter, 8 the dormant seed, 3 spring burst, 4 branching, 9 peak summer, 2 late summer, 7 harvest, 6 pre-winter cutting back. 5 is the center, not walked.
A period's hexagram is its own trigram over the trigram of the cycle that contains it: day over month, month over year, year over great year.
On a hexad line, the destination trigram goes over the origin: one hexagram per line. The inversion is held loosely, a side note at most.

5 has no trigram and no hexagram of its own. It inherits the trigram of the nearest higher cycle that is not 5; a chain of 5s keeps looking up. The two lines touching 5 are built on the day from that trigram, destination over origin: 8 → 5 is the inherited trigram over Gen, 5 → 7 is Dui over the inherited trigram. Nothing is doubled.
The center is where the larger cycle reaches down into the smaller one; the inheritance is that idea as a figure rule.
Moving lines are always the difference between two resolved figures. No fixed tables.
In the interval traces yin becomes yang, never the reverse: 1↔4 and 2↔8 move line 6 (completed from outside); 5↔7 moves whatever the parent makes it.

Each line has an element verb, what crosses it: nourish 1→4, break 4→2, inherit 2→8, keep 8→5, reflect 5→7, shape 7→1. Lines use a shorter template (what crosses, verb, hexagram, two failure modes) and carry no shadows of their own.
The triangle points take their own trigram doubled: 51 Shock at 3, 1 The Dynamic at 6, 30 Clarity at 9, at any scale.
Readings come only from The Gnostic Book of Changes through Stella: judgment, superior-man line, editor's notes, changing lines.
Field: the period's hexagram as the page builds it, the period's trigram over its container's. Shown in every profile.

Shi (勢, momentum, the tendency of a situation): the field's course in time, the moving lines between this period's field and the previous or next period's at the same level. What the rim shows, and the hexad along its wiring; it gets the name, nothing else changes.

Ji (機, the pivot, the incipient moment): the native in the field, the moving lines between the native hexagram and the field at the same level and moment. Read field → native: the field is the given, the native the response; the text is the field's at those lines.

The native hexagram: the personal number's trigram at a level over the house of the natal month number at the same level, ki(natal month − global + 5); a house of 5 resolves by inheritance. A construction, not traditional Nine Star Ki; the inner and outer trigram convention is classical I Ching. Not built for the Global profile.
Ki years run Lichun to Lichun; months begin when the Sun crosses 15° of each sign. Every level counts down by one and never resets at a seam.
Seven levels: great age, Ki Age, great year, year, month, day, hour. Day octave: the day trigram above the month's.

Your position: natal 5.9.1. Li 9 year, Kan 1 month; the year rolls to Kan 1 at Lichun, 3 Feb 2027. Personal great year 9 Li inside the global gate 1 Kan, Lichun 2022 to 2034. The nine-month arc runs 63 → 64.

Warrior = force; Gardener = cultivation and receptivity; both held under the King, the higher vision.

Four functions: supply, cultivate, boundary, force. Four patterns: Wall, Water, Mountain, River; the Ocean collects everything and keeps nothing. A pattern is two functions; a function named by itself is a single function, and the first member of each interval trace is one: 1 Supply, 2 Cultivate, completed into River at 4 and Mountain at 8.
Shadow Warrior: Judge / Martyr. Shadow Gardener: Over-Engineer / Paralyzer.

Shadow poles are true Jungian opposites; two compulsions is one trait with two outlets.

On the hexad, names are figures doing the point's failure, not the point itself and not an adjective. On the Triforce, shadows are conditions. Strong, concise, not trite. No "gloss"; a second name beside a figure is interchangeable with it (Dragon, the Hoarder).
Headlines are one capitalised word naming the point's place in this system, not its trigram: Potential, Field, Power, River, Delta, Will, Lake, Mountain, Clarity.
Six parts to a pair: trigrams, line change, shadow axis, functions, stacked hexagrams, tarot. Plus the practice line. Lines get the shorter template.
Points are the numbers 1 to 9. No solfège, no "note".

No "charge", "deposit" or "return". The two kinds of trace: the interval trace acts within its own octave (1→4, 2→8, 5→7); the octave trace extends into the next (4→2, 8→5, 7→1). "Echo pair" is retired in favor of interval trace.

"Potential" for 1, not "the depths" or "the well". "Delta" for 5, not "the hub". "Power" for 3, not Thunder or Shock. "Will" for 6, not Discernment or Courage. 1's shadows are the Timid Boy and the Blue Belt; Over-Engineer and Unmoored are what they do, not their names. 2's passive shadow is Stagnation, not Hoarfrost; 2's Balanced is Generative, not Calm.

Trace is the verb for every link, never feeds or fed by. 1 traces to 4; 4 traces back to 1; 4 is traced from 1. On the day: the 1 day leaves a trace, the 4 day traces it. From stigmergy (Grassé, stigma + ergon, work by the mark): the trace is left in the medium, it stimulates rather than instructs, it is read by the same agent later, and it decays unless reinforced.
The trace is your word for what a day leaves behind; it can be either shadow or the middle way.

Jungian and Ki-nature metaphors only. Nothing new-agey ("what are you holding" is out).

entries.t: The one pole we figured out is the fear, or over-engineering; the other is the reckless, the more impulsive side of it. And then we have courage, which is someone who's willing to face fear, but with preparation. In terms of the Gardener aspect this is the supply. It's an internal supply, deep in the water. And the supply internally is asking: do you have the courage, can you face what's down there? Maybe on water days a deep meditation is warranted.

Kan is stillness on the outside with one firm thing in the middle. Sitting still and going under is the only way to find the firm thing, and it is the opposite of both shadows at once: the fearful one won't sit, the reckless one won't sit still.

If you look at Jung's shadow poles, they are typically opposites. If both are compulsion that defeats the purpose. If you over-engineer because you're afraid, then you are literally not engaging with the thing because you're afraid, but the structure is built around it. The impulsive or reckless side is the opposite of that: there is no structure, there is no thought, it's just blind engagement, which is guaranteed to have a higher failure rate. Which is not always bad. But in its shadow side it ends up being a lost thread, because you can't connect impulsive threads.

A mooring is what ties a boat in place, the rope and the post it's fastened to. Unmoored means cut loose, no line holding you to anything fixed. The Over-Engineer is all mooring and never leaves the dock. The Unmoored dives with no line, and the thread is lost. A boat with no mooring at 1 is a boat going wherever the wind blows at 4.

I love the idea of the one line closing, and how the water stays underneath and the top expands up. Which is what happens in the tree: if there are proper roots, proper water, the energy flows upward into the stem, into the leaves, which then can be healthy and flexible. The middle way can take a hundred faces. This is a primordial archetype which can be applied to a myriad of things in life; the symbolism is what helps us understand it.

The Over-Engineer never lets the top line turn. The structure stays in place, so Kan stays Kan: yin on top, the firm thing still buried. Four comes and the trigram hasn't changed. The Unmoored is the other error: the top line turns, but there's no bottom line left to hold. Picture the yin at the bottom turning too, so you get Li, all surface and a hollow center, or the whole trigram going to Qian, a tree with no root. The middle way isn't a line position; it's the fact that exactly one line moves and it's the right one. The two shadows are zero lines moving, or too many.

The High Priestess is the water itself, the mystery. She sits between the pillars with the veil behind her and the scroll half hidden: pure yin surface with one firm thing concealed, which is Kan's shape exactly. Her concealed thing is the scroll in her lap, the law, the whole knowledge, finished and exact, and you can only read the edge of it. Behind her the veil with pomegranates hides the water that runs under everything in the deck; every later card with water in it is drawing from what's behind her curtain. You only get the piece you're prepared to carry up.
Dang, that's really good.

The Fool is card zero and the Magician is card one. The Fool carries everything in a bag on a stick, unsorted; the Magician has opened that bag, laid its contents on the table, and picked up the wand. Two readings exist. The common one is the Fool's journey: he meets each card as a teacher and carries on, still the Fool, collecting. The structural one is that the Fool is the substance and the cards are its states: zero becomes one. For water's journey to 4 the second is the one that works, because that's exactly what a trigram change is: the same three lines, one state becoming the next. Kan to Xun isn't water meeting wood and carrying on, it's water becoming wood.
That's what I like better. Yeah, let's do that one.
The timid boy, and the blue belt.

A blue belt is the second rank, the first one you earn. White is given to you for showing up. Blue means you've trained long enough to have real technique, you can beat an untrained person, and you've started to roll with people who can hurt you. It's the rank where the most people quit and the rank with the worst reputation for injuring training partners, because skill has outrun judgment. Someone who has earned the right to be confident and has not yet earned the right to be sure. In Jung's terms it's inflation: one real contact with the unconscious and the ego thinks it's initiated. In Gurdjieff's, the man who had one moment of self-remembering and now believes he's awake. In the deck, the Fool who has forgotten he's the Fool. Every blue belt has a real win behind him, which is why he's seductive in a way the timid boy never is. He drifts at 4 because he came up with momentum, not with the thing, and momentum is the wind.

Timid is the state; over-engineering is one thing the timid do with it. The timid boy at the water can freeze, wander off, keep asking if it's safe, or build a boat. Over-engineering is the last one: fear turned into preparation that never ends, the Gardener's version of timidity. Both poles are failures of preparation against the depth; timid and rash is what they feel like from inside.
Potential is good, let's go with that. And "What's under the surface?"

Kun is three yin lines, the mother, the earth itself. No hidden line anywhere, nothing concealed, which is the opposite of 1. Kan had one firm thing hidden in the dark. Kun has nothing firm at all, and that's its power: it receives everything and holds its shape. Southwest, late summer, fertile or scorched ground, and that fork is the whole point: the same field either grows the crop or burns.
The two poles of 2 are Jung's devouring mother, who holds everything and releases nothing, and the abandoning mother, who refuses to receive anything.

Three things, and I'd been sliding between them. The field is the ground, not the crop: it's 2 itself, worked all summer, so it's the capacity to receive. The Empress doesn't own what grows on it; she is the condition for growing. The seed is the one thing that came off that field with a future in it. Everything else gets eaten or rots, and that's what it was for. The light I'd drop; it was muddying things. The lantern on the card is just the container, the Hermit's firm top line, the cap that keeps the seed from scattering. So the field is 2's ground, the seed is what's selected from it, and the lantern is 8's hold on it.

He doesn't inherit the last seed because the farm dwindled. He inherits one seed because that's all a seed ever is. The hundreds of fruits were never going to carry forward; they were the yield, and yield gets spent. That's what 7 was for. What's left after the harvest is always small, and that's not a loss, it's the shape of the thing.

It is the greatness held underneath. Modesty, temperance. The mountain of work, say an artist's 10,000 hours to become a master: when they scribble something on a napkin and it's the most beautiful thing ever, it's the result of those 10,000 hours, the mountain that's under the earth. And the other one is the thing on full display, but the only thing left.

2 The Magnetic. Other titles: The Receptive, Field, The Flow, Responsive Service, Yin, The Bearer. Editor's judgment: the ego bears the burden of the Work; success is found in compliance with the will of the Self. The Superior Man supports the Work through its many transformations. "If the superior man takes the initiative, he goes astray," supplemented by the image of a docile mare which uncomplainingly bears its load. The editor quotes Case on Daleth, the Door: "I am the fruitful womb whence all creatures have their birth." Daleth is the Empress's own letter.

At her best the Empress does nothing and everything grows. Waite: the fruitful mother of thousands, the door by which entrance is obtained into this life. She sits; the wheat ripens at her feet; she holds the scepter and doesn't use it. The problem with Calm: the abandoning mother looks calm from outside. The Balanced word has to exclude both poles, the way Courage excludes both the timid boy and the blue belt. Generative passes: the Smotherer thinks she's generative and nothing comes up because she keeps digging it out; the Stagnant field is left to rot; only the Balanced field produces. Erikson's seventh stage is generativity against stagnation, and he names its two failures: overextension and rejectivity. That's the Smotherer and the abandoning mother in a clinician's words.
Generative is the right word. And let's replace Hoarfrost. It's not that it's frozen, it's that she's left the field to rot. Stagnation is a good one for that.

entries.t: The sprout runs on what the seed stored. No leaf yet, so no income, only savings. All that energy is spent on one job: reach the light before the savings run out. The force is huge, the body is frail, and it gets one try. That's 3: a fixed charge of energy with a single purpose, and the vices are about spending the charge. Spend it all at once: the sprout that shoots up fast and thin, no root under it, and topples the first windy day. Refuse to spend it: the seed that keeps its reserve underground and never cracks; the charge doesn't keep, it rots in the shell. Between them the sprout that spends exactly enough to break the surface, then starts making leaves and paying its own way. Which is what 51 says in different words: adjust the tempo, the goal stays.

entries.t: Argos, Greek argós, "without work," faith without works. Odysseus's dog in the story didn't fail; he's the one creature in Ithaca who stays faithful and knows Odysseus on sight. The failure, if you read him as a figure, is in what the waiting cost. He was a hunting dog bred for speed, and he spent twenty years on a dung heap doing nothing, because the one thing that would have made him move never came. When it finally did, all he had left was the recognition, and then he died. The force was real, and it was spent entirely on waiting for permission from outside. That's the passive 3: faithful to the goal, and he let the whole charge go waiting for the mentor to arrive rather than acting as if he already had. entries.t: The Triforce is three golden triangles making one, each held by a goddess: Power, Wisdom, Courage. The lore that fits: it grants a wish to whoever touches it, but if the heart holding it isn't balanced among the three, it splits apart and the person keeps only the piece they're strongest in. Ganon gets Power alone. That's the guardrail from your own origin notes: the higher centers won't open until personality is mature, because premature access is dangerous. Kept as a side note under the name, not applied to the names themselves.

One isn't a complete picture, and that's correct, not a gap. Your four patterns, Wall, Water, Mountain, River, are each two functions together. River is supply plus cultivate. So 1 is supply alone, a function, not yet a pattern. It only becomes a pattern at 4 when cultivate joins it. Which maps onto the whole hexad: the first member of every pair is a single function, the second completes it into one of the four patterns. The fact that there isn't a landscape word for 1 on its own is the point: a function on its own hasn't taken a shape yet.

Taken literally, the Fool steps off the cliff and the water is where he lands. So the one day isn't a chosen dive, it's a fall, and the courage question is really whether you accept where you landed. Then the Magician isn't who he turns into; he's who meets him there, the one who's done this before and knows what's in the bag. That's conscience as the memory of last time. The Magician is the four day reading the one day's note. In the recursion he's the previous octave's four, or at the month level the earlier month's. The two cards are the same person at two different times.
Nice.

59 Dispersion, Xun over Kan: wind blowing across water and breaking it into ripples, dissolving what was frozen or clotted. The king approaches his temple; it furthers one to cross the great water. The healthy 4 reading 1: the wind moves what the water held, and the move is outward, across. 48 The Well, Kan over Xun: the wooden bucket going down into the well and bringing water up. The town may change but the well does not; if the rope doesn't reach, or the jug breaks, misfortune. Too short a rope is the Timid Boy, a broken jug the Blue Belt.

One's two shadows are about depth: won't go in and won't come out. Four's two shadows are about direction: won't move and moves without choosing. And they match across the link. The one who never went under becomes the Paralyzer with no root to stand on; the one who never surfaced becomes the Drifter with water but no channel. That gives a recursion test: if the shadows at 1 predict the shadows at 4, a bad 1 day should produce a recognizable bad 4 day three days later, and you can check that in the log.

entries.t: You said if you lived a four day with two in mind, the cycle would continue, and that's the practice for 4. The Magician at 4 isn't just passing the test, he's growing what will fall. What he makes under the sun is what the field gets. So the question on a four day is less "did I pass" and more "what am I producing that's worth the ground."

5 has no fixed trigram and borrows the current month's figure, which makes it a delta point, where the day touches a larger time scale. Worked example: Gen to Kan, hexagram 39, lines 5 and 6. The moving lines measure the distance between what was kept at 8 and what the larger cycle demands, and the Gnostic line texts are the prescription.

The classical Ki reading of 5: everything flies around you and nothing moves for you. It's described as pivotal: what you've built comes to you, what you've neglected comes to you too. Absorb, in Haner's word. A year to stay put and let things arrive rather than go after them. So the classical relationship is earth generating metal: the center that absorbs everything feeds the lake that reflects it.

What you just said just kind of says it outright. Not settled necessarily, because we have a whole template to go over, but I think we're finding the seam here, which to me is what classically it represents and what I'm trying to make it do.

Classically 5 and 7 are a stretch of the walk: you sit in the center, things arrive, then two years later you enjoy and reflect on what arrived, with 6 between them. In yours, 5 and 7 are a pair on the inner lines with 6 skipped: 5 is a delta that injects the parent, 7 reads what 5 injected. That's a wire, not a stretch of road. The classical 5 absorbs because it's empty; your 5 inherits because it's empty. Same emptiness, but one fills from life and the other fills from the figure above.

The Divine Child is the boy form of the King. He's the source of life and blessing, at the center of everything, cared for because of what he is rather than what he does. His active shadow is the High Chair Tyrant: demands to be served, throws down what's offered, no gratitude, hurts the ones who feed him. His passive shadow is the Weakling Prince: no life force of his own, wants to be carried, gets attention through helplessness and secretly manipulates everyone to look after him. The High Chair Tyrant matures into the Tyrant at 7: the boy who throws down what he's given becomes the man who seizes it. The Weakling Prince matures into the Princess: the boy who got carried becomes the one who runs things by never lifting anything.

I think the boy forms fit five. It works for now; I might come up with different names later. They represent what they do. My own image of 5 is the yin-yang: balance holding still, opposites holding each other's seeds.

Five, to me, is the nascent externalized karmic reconciliation. Almost like three, it's something outside of ourselves where we are shown something about our hand, about our time, about our cycle. What we choose to do with it becomes either the high chair tyrant or the weakling prince, where we try to force it into submission or we do nothing about it. And the alternative route is to give blessings, for that to evolve into six. When five is done correctly, six's role is pretty clear. Or five brings the larger cycle into context, maybe even judging the eight against the larger cycle.

If 5 is about karma, what better judge than Capricorn, Saturn and time itself? Three cards, meant to be read together. And the hexagram: it's the trigram of the larger cycle paired with whatever it's interacting with in the system, so 8 and 7.

5 is about unblocking, whatever that means in the moment, mental, emotional, physical, for what is coming through to land. It is tending to oneself, not pushing outward. I was pushing during the 8 and 9 hours, but when my hour shifted into 1, at the pinnacle of 9, it dawned on me that what I really need to be doing is unblocking myself, my environment, so that I can receive, so that the reflection is clear at 7 and the discernment at 6 rings clear and true.
Qian at 6 is late autumn, pre-winter, not summer. 6 is the selection of the next seed, not expansion.
6 Stress, Qian over Kan, read on the live 6 day: hold the work pressure and the draw toward this study in stable tension rather than forcing a resolution. The editor's title is Stress, not Conflict.

entries.t: 1 The Dynamic. Qian doubled. Other titles: The Creative, Heaven, Force, The Key, Primal Power, The Life Force, Kundalini, God the Father. Judgment: the Dynamic is the life force itself. The Superior Man tirelessly furthers the Great Work of Transformation. Editor: a dragon appears in every line except the third. In Western myth the dragon is the adversary the hero must conquer to get the treasure; the Chinese regard it positively, dragons provide rain and rule the ocean. Wilhelm compares the dragon to the electricity in a thunderstorm: as lightning it destroys, harnessed it does useful work. When the dragon remains unconquered in the depths of the unconscious, the life force rules our lives autonomously and we become passive vehicles for random desires; a life is created by chance and circumstance. When one begins the Work, one assumes the role of the hero or warrior who battles the dragon to bring it under his will. If one can control the life force, the treasure is obtained, which amounts to a higher level of consciousness. The first two hexagrams must be studied together: Heaven and Earth, Force and Form. As consciousness is to the body, so Force is to Form.
