Self-Righteousness: the ego's will passed off as the Self's, "I know what's right" with the knowing coming from the wrong seat, so the cut is really the ego protecting itself and calling it conviction. Indulgence: the ego's appetite with the Self forgotten entirely. Rejected on the way: the Arrogant Dragon (hexagram 1's own top line, the dragon that flies too high and has cause to repent), the Passenger (the editor's "passive vehicle for random desires"), the Zealot, the Prodigal, the Reaper.

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: Where 6 sits: not the cave, that's 8, and not the harvest party, that's 7. It's the discernment of what to carry into winter after the party, plus the carrying. First half readiness, second half the action. A battle against winter. The fight is sustained will against dispersal, drift, inner entropy; not against the ego, which is the warrior, and not against imbalance, which is the symptom. The dragon is internal at 6; an unconquered dragon at 6 sits down and hoards at 8.

Haner's Seven is the Artist: charming, gracious, aware of what's going on around, sensitive to nuance and detail, always refining. The failure she names is denial, pretending things are fine for years, and under stress denying your own needs to keep things lovely for everyone else. Her line that matters: Sevens maintain such poise that nobody sees anything is wrong, and it's only if things start to go wrong in ways the Seven can't control that the ripples appear on the lake. Her image for 7 is the Princess, the longing to live the good life and be taken care of. The Yoshikawa line is simpler: autumn, west, harvest and pleasure, reward for previous work; enjoy and celebrate but watch for excess; youngest daughter, joy, beauty, natural sensuality. The Gnostic text on Dui: in Joy, the lake doubled, the superior man encourages the conversation of friends and the stimulus of their common practice; in Influence, lake on the mountain, he receives people by virtue of emptiness; in Following, thunder in the lake, he goes inside and rests when the sun goes down. The lake is open at the top, empty enough to receive, and it's the figure for speech and shared practice, not private pleasure.

Haner's shadow is the ripple on the surface, and the I Ching's virtue is emptiness. The lake works when it's still and open; it fails when it's either full of itself or disturbed. Put the three together and 7 has a clear job: be a still, open surface. It receives by emptiness, shows what the sky put in it, and shares that out loud. The harvest is partly the seeing and partly the telling.

Waite on the Chariot: the King in his triumph, the victory that creates kingship. Outwardly active, inwardly still, steered by equanimity rather than force. The Hierophant explicitly receives and shows a higher order; the Chariot is that order in motion. Reveler and Smoother, then Grasper and Smoother, were rejected as adjective-like and trite.

For seven, the tyrant and the princess are pretty good, and king is the integrated form. The tyrant is the one who tries to grasp at the meaning in a manipulative way, in a controlling way. And the princess is the one who just smooths it over despite knowing what's held beneath: passively taking control without doing anything of substance.

Seven is what's left after the sixth shock, and it is to some degree clarity, because it's what has been stripped away, and then you can see clearly in it the next right thing to do. That's what the king energy is. The chariot means to reflect on the water and carry it into the next phase.

Li is the seeing itself, light on everything, which is why 9 is where you see one clear question. Seven isn't the light, it's the surface the light lands on. A lake reflects because it's still, and it's still because six cut away everything that was churning it. So the reflection is what's visible once nothing's moving: the obvious thing, whether or not it's comfortable. And the trace is naming it. Not "I saw clearly," but the sentence. So the seven-day note has two parts: what the reflection said, and what you did about it.

In practice, smaller than meditation: don't add anything new to the pile, look at what was held, notice what's obvious about it now that the week has stopped churning. Then do the next concrete step the obvious thing implies, without arguing with the picture or improving it. The Tyrant's version is "now let me use this clarity to fix five other things." The Princess is "good, I see it, I'll note it for later."

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: 5 → 7 settled: the lake reflects what 5 inherited. 7's imagery, the lake filling and the king leaving the shore, flagged as shaky on 25 Oct, no longer is.

Kun is the mother, Gen is the youngest son, not the eldest. Zhen, thunder, is the eldest, with the firm line at the bottom; Gen has it at the top, the one born latest. That changes the Hermit picture. The Empress is the mother with everything growing, and the Hermit is her youngest, the one who was there when the field emptied. The older sons took the force and the movement and went out into the world. The youngest stays, gets the house, and inherits what's left when she's done. That's why he's old on the card despite being the youngest: he's carrying what the mother made for longer than anyone. His firm top line is the one thing she wasn't, a cap, and that's the only thing he adds to her.

What survives her is the ground she made. Cultivation isn't the crop, it's soil that can hold a seed through a winter without her standing over it. So what the Empress hands the Hermit is a ground that's already been taught to keep things alive. His lantern isn't his own light, it's hers with the field removed. Her yes to everything becomes his yes to one thing. The Hermit is cultivate with no sun, which is the first time it becomes a pattern. He's proof that she worked. If he can keep the seed, the ground was good. If it dies in his lantern, that's scorched ground.

15 and 23 are the same single yang line in two positions. In 15 it's buried under the earth, the mastery nobody can see. In 23 it's the one thing left standing on top after everything else fell away. The seed hidden, and the seed exposed. 15 is the field with the mountain already in it; the seed isn't something 8 adds later.

entries.s: Shadow side of two and eight
entries.t: The Dragon lives in the mountain but is not the mountain; he keeps all of it. The Barrow is the burial mound, the grave: it keeps nothing. Stillness between them. Warden, Deserter, Locust, Ghost, Blight and Fallow were turned down; the rule that came out of it was a figure doing the failure, not a description of a place.

entries.s: Shadow side of two and eight
entries.t: Powerful images, definitely remember that.

23 Disintegration, Gen over Kun: do not act; the superior man stabilizes his responses. Line 6: the large fruit still uneaten, an accrual of karma; the carriage, a new way of going. 15 Temperance, Kun over Gen: a dynamic, magnetic balance of forces; the mountain hidden beneath the earth.

An 8 Mountain day over water: stillness sitting atop the receptive. The 2-day trace, followed back two cycles, read 7 Discipline turning to 4 Inexperience on the top line: something mobilised earlier in the month and not closed by the follow-through it needed, the same figure across two cycles, an unresolved loop.

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: Dragon and the Hoarder, Barrow and the Recluse: interchangeable names, figure and feel. The Hoarder keeps instead of carries; the Recluse is the mound of the dead. The quality of an 8 day: choose one mountain. 52, keeping the back still. Haner's 8 year is the caterpillar in the cocoon; her first-number 8 is the Transformer; in the mountain there is a cave, and the cave holds the treasure.
8 is about tending to one thing with great care.

Fire at 9: Li, the Clinging; yin held inside yang; light that exists only in relation to what it burns. Consciousness as the seeing, not a stage of the seen. 9 is the source and the destination, the arm; 3 and 6 are the hands.

The Ocean collects everything but keeps nothing. Rivers move toward the ocean with purpose. Year 9 delivers sight, not a harvest. The one thing from my 9 year that hasn't dimmed is curiosity, and building things for their own sake. From nine lived years: 9's clarity is itself activating and leads to being spread too thin; at 9 the job is to see one clear question, not act.

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: 9 isn't a stage. Every hexad point does something: grows, keeps, reflects. Li doesn't do, it sees. And the editor's instruction on 30 is the opposite of what fire suggests: not blaze, but docility, the cow. The power originates somewhere else and your job at 9 is not to interfere with it. Which is self-remembering exactly: the arrow back to "I, here." The sun and moon line is the hexad and the triangle in one sentence: growing things are the hexad, they aren't luminous, they're lit. The Self is the sun, 9, and the ego is what grows under it. So 9 doesn't appear in the wiring because it's the light the wiring is seen by. That's why the triangle never touches the hexagon. Then the net: clarity as comprehension, a mesh that catches insight. 9 is the King's actual seat; he lives here, the hexad is where he works. The failure is sleep, not being there when the light's on.

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: Sure. For now.

The Sun: a naked child on a white horse under a full sun, sunflowers behind a low wall. Nothing hidden, nothing carried, everything lit; illumination, the plain seeing of a child. That is 9 as what it does. The World: a dancer inside a wreath, the four fixed creatures at the corners; completion that is also the start, the whole seen from outside. The wreath is a zero, the Fool's number, so it closes the deck back onto its beginning. That is 9 as where it sits.

Gurdjieff's enneagram has three bridge links, 4→2, 8→5, 7→1, alongside the three echo pairs, and together they make one continuous six-link circuit. You asked for this to be held and integrated, and on 23 Oct revised the rules so the hexad is one chain, not three pairs plus a bridge.

The editor says 47 and 48, the Well, are the same figure flipped. In 47 you're on the surface of a dry lake bed and the water is below you, out of reach. In 48 you're at the well, drawing from that same water. Nothing was lost; it changed level. So 7 → 1 isn't a loss link: the lake empties because the harvest sinks down into the source the next one draws from. Water over the lake is the lake the water has left; in 60 the water is below the lake, so the lake holds.

47 Oppression. Other titles: Exhaustion, Dried Up, "Actions speak louder than words." Editor's judgment: with enough will, success can be won; the answer lies beyond the realm of reason and logic. The Superior Man stakes everything he's got on his will to succeed. The image is a dry lake bed; the Well is its upside-down image, an unending source flowing from deep beneath the surface. To be under Oppression is to be cut off from sustenance although there is water down below. The lower trigram of Peril goes on to the upper trigram of Cheerfulness, which 60 also turns on: a light heart under hard conditions. Lines 2 and 5 mention sacrifice; sincerity is the condition. Line 1: one sits oppressed under a bare tree and strays into a gloomy valley; for three years one sees nothing. Wing: a trap of your own making, discouragement. The editor: self-pity, lack of clarity, some illusion prevails; sometimes it means you have misunderstood a previous hexagram.

The King Wen sequence pairs almost every hexagram with its upside-down twin: 3 and 4, 5 and 6, 11 and 12, up to 63 and 64. The eight that look the same flipped, Qian and Kun, 27 and 28, 29 and 30, 61 and 62, are paired by inverting every line instead. So 47 and 48 are doing what the sequence always does. What nobody has explained is why the twenty-eight pairs sit in the order they do. Three live readings: a narrative, which the Sequence commentary tells and which can be fitted to any order; a hidden structure, where there are real partial results, more line-count symmetries than chance would give, but no generating rule; or historical accident. The evidence sits between the last two. Which, for your work, is the interesting case: a fully solved order would be a machine, a random one would be noise, and one with partial pattern is exactly what the hexad is: structure that can't lift itself.
In practice it's literally just a seed. It's just something I write down that I read on the one day.

Yes. The whole 47-48 business is just saying why that works: the sentence isn't on the surface anymore when 1 arrives; it's the thing under the water you go in for. The only part that's really a practice is at 7: don't keep rereading it. Write it, act once, close the note. That's the floor opening. If you keep it visible it's a lake, not a well.

In stigmergy the trace is the whole mechanism. Grassé coined the word in 1959 watching termites: stigma, a mark, plus ergon, work. A termite drops a pellet; the pellet, not the termite, is what makes the next termite drop one beside it. Nobody instructs anybody. Ant trails are the other case: pheromone laid down by whoever passed, read by whoever comes next, and it evaporates unless it's reinforced. Three things in that were already yours: the trace is left in the medium, not handed to anyone; it stimulates, it doesn't instruct; and the agent who reads it is usually the same one who left it, later, which is self-remembering across time. The evaporation is the part you didn't have: an unread trace decays, and that's the difference between a loop and a spiral in the medium itself.

Trace comes from Latin tractus, drawn: a trace is a line drawn, and to trace is either to draw the line or to follow it. Same word for the one who leaves it and the one who comes after. A tracing is the copy you make by following lines through paper. The Magician at 4 holds a tracing of the Priestess's scroll, not the scroll.

Everything moves forward and there is always a trace. That is just how lived time is: internally we process it in the hexad pattern, externally it's all just moving to the next moment, the next hour, the next minute. The spiral pattern is moving forward but we can stay trapped in internal processes that feel like we aren't moving forward even though time is. And so the traces that are left behind are both contained within their own octave and also the next. 9 is the great culminator of all, as it gathers and disperses what was held in the cycle. The fruit bearing new seeds. The seeds themselves are products of the past and contain within them a blueprint, but no one seed is the same. Even though we go through nested 9-step cycles, no one spiral is the same. The trace that acts within its octave and the trace that extends to the next: it's almost like a harmonic. Interval trace and octave trace.

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: 46 Pushing Upward, Kun over Xun. Other titles: Rising, Ascending, Sprouting from the Earth, Organic Growth. Editor's judgment: ascend in accordance with the will of the Self; turn toward clarity. The Superior Man grows a little every day. The image is a plant in the earth gradually pushing upward toward the sun. "An advance to the south is fortunate" means that as all plants turn southward toward the sun, their source of nourishment, so should we turn toward the light and clarity of the great man, the Self within us. There is no such thing as instant enlightenment; the stories of instant satori are the final few moments' resolution after a lifetime of slow and patient devotion. The Work progresses at the pace of a tree. He calls this growth an accumulation of countless "gathering togethers," which is 45, the hexagram 46 is the upside-down image of, and closes with Origen: "thou art a second little world, and the sun and moon are within thee, and also the stars."

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: What crosses from 4 to 2 is the seed, and 46 is the seed after it's landed. The text's whole weight is on pace. And "advance to the south" names the direction: on the Lo Shu, 4 is southeast, 2 is southwest, and 9 fire sits between them. The sprout doesn't push back toward 4 where it came from; it pushes toward 9. The ground is holding it but the sun is pulling it. 45 Gathering Together is Dui over Kun, lake on the earth, so 7's residue is in 2's soil too, not just 4's seed; the field gets fed from two directions. Failure modes from 46: wanting instant enlightenment, pushing up fast and hollow; and the sprout turning the wrong way, back toward where it came from, the field refusing disturbance. 20 Contemplation sits behind it as the condition: the Magician on the tower who had to actually let it fall, not just contemplate. Preparation without the act and nothing's in the ground.

entries.s: Reflecting on the system's past days
entries.t: Stacking rule for a line: destination over origin, one hexagram per line, the inversion held loosely. Element verbs for what crosses, concept only, not used language: feed, break, inherit, keep, reflect, shape. Lines take a shorter template and carry no shadows of their own. 2 → 8: "do not act" means don't grasp; the Hermit inherits only the one fruit. 8 → 5: 5 is the one place the day touches the larger cycle and 8 is the virtue that opens it; if 8 isn't lived, 5 balances you from outside.

Time is the rim: the circle, the path. The laws are separate from the names. The rim is the path of time, the hexad is the Law of Seven, the triangle is the Law of Three. 4 does not trace to the Delta; the River reaching the Delta is the path of time, not the hexad. Is the hexad a path at all? More of a harmonic process. And the triangle is transformative.

1 into 2. The water meets ground. Whatever was under the surface stops being a question and sinks into the field, where it becomes capacity rather than depth. You stop diving and start receiving. Earth holds water, so this is potential being given a shape to sit in. From outside it looks like nothing happening; that's the refusal beat, and it's correct.

2 into 3. The field is still, and then something comes up through it that you didn't plant. The seed splits and the shoot breaks the surface, wood breaking earth. Receiving produced it, but it arrives with force you didn't supply and at a tempo you didn't set. That's why it feels like an event, and why it's the mentor: it comes from outside the ground you were tending.

3 into 4. Thunder becomes wind. Same wood, but the yang burst goes yin and flexible. Power with no direction is wildfire; power given a channel is a river. This is where you choose which way the loan runs, and the trace back to 1 is what you choose by: you point the river at what the water held. The tests begin because you now have a direction that can be wrong.

4 into 5. The river reaches the end of itself. It meets earth again, but this earth is bigger than the river: the delta, where your current drops what it carried into a body you don't control. The day touches the month. Everything you've been steering since 4 gets handed to a scale that was turning before you started.

5 into 6. Earth makes metal. Out of what the larger cycle showed you, a blade. You're standing in the delta with what you carried and what landed, and the one thing left is to decide what goes on into winter. Nothing outside does this part; the shock at 3 was given, this one isn't. The ordeal is that it's yours.

6 into 7. Metal to metal: the sword becomes the mirror. Once the cut is made the surface goes still, and what the will kept shows itself plainly for the first time. The reward isn't new; it's the same thing you've carried since 4, finally visible.

7 into 8. The lake drains into the mountain. Metal goes back to its mother, earth. The reflection is done with, and the one thing that lasted is carried into the cave and set down, not planted, not touched. The road back, in the hour before dawn.

8 into 9. The sun comes up on the mountain. What was kept in the dark is seen from above with the whole octave around it, and seeing is all 9 does. The fruit is ripe and carries seeds, and none of them are the seed you started with.

9 into 1. The sun goes down into the water. Clarity becomes potential again; the thing seen sinks under the surface and waits. The lake's sentence from 7 is already down there. The next dive starts one turn higher, into water that already holds something.

Not pinned, mine: Time's path barely runs the generative cycle. Of its nine steps, three are controlling (water held, earth broken, river swallowed), two return child to mother (lake to mountain, mountain to sun), two stay in one element, and only 5 into 6 generates. The generating runs on the hexad. Time mostly constrains; the pattern underneath is what grows.

The circle is the process: drawn closed because the end is the beginning one level up, 9 and 0 coincide; from above a ring, from the side a spiral. The rim is time: the order in which things happen, nothing more. The hexagon is the wiring, from 1/7 = 0.142857 repeating; every seventh is the same six digits rotated, which is why the six lines form one closed loop; 3, 6, 9 never appear. It says which stages are feeding which regardless of when they occur; left alone it loops at the same level forever; structure but no force. The triangle touches the rim but never the hexagon: if the shocks were part of the wiring the process could self-start, and Gurdjieff's whole claim is that it cannot. "The rim is where things happen, the hexagon is why they happen in the shape they do, the triangle is what makes them happen at all."

The 1/7 wiring mechanically: long division gives digit and remainder, 1 r3, 4 r2, 2 r6, 8 r4, 5 r5, 7 r1, back to start. Every leftover 1 to 6 exactly once; nothing wasted, nothing escapes; 7 itself never appears because it is the measure, not a stage. "1 produces 4" means the incompleteness of stage 1 is the material of stage 4. The circuit is perfectly efficient at recycling its own residue, which is exactly why it cannot lift itself. Gurdjieff gave only the arithmetic and the food example; the echo reading is defensible interpretation, not scripture.

The Law of Seven and the intervals: the major scale has two half-steps, and Gurdjieff treated these literally. Any process stalls at those two positions, about a third and two thirds through, and unshocked it bends, eventually curving back toward the opposite of its origin: revolutions to tyrannies, diets to binges. In the food octave, food enters at do, stalls at mi-fa, and is carried by air, the automatic first shock. Impressions enter and die at do unless the second shock, self-remembering at the moment of receiving the impression, is made consciously. The engineering reading: failure is not randomly distributed; it concentrates at two fixed points. Design the shock in: fuses, expansion joints, crumple zones. Pre-install the third force, a review, an outside deadline, a person whose job is to be the shock, rather than hoping the mentor shows up.

Forces are qualities: active, passive, reconciling. They rotate around the circle; every stage has one. Pushing harder against passive resistance only strengthens the standoff; the question at a stall is "what is the third thing that is neither push nor resistance?" Points are positions: at 3 and 6 what is needed is always the reconciling force, and 9 is where it comes from. The night-and-day image: the sun is not day, the shadow is not night; the Earth turning is what produces the pair, and dawn and dusk are where the third force becomes visible. Not a duality, a trinity.

Hero's journey compressed to nine beats: 9 ordinary world and return with the elixir; 1 the call; 2 the refusal; 3 the mentor, the first shock, given; 4 tests, allies, enemies; 5 approach to the inmost cave; 6 the ordeal, death and rebirth, the second shock, made; 7 the reward; 8 the road back. Inner lines as plot: the call shapes the tests; the tests expose the refusal; the refusal determines the road back; the hero carries home what they first ran from. Campbell's departure, initiation, return is the Law of Three. The agency gap: in Campbell the shocks arrive; in Gurdjieff the second must be made. Roughly the difference between a story about a hero and the practice of being one.

Self-remembering makes more sense when you consider the particle and wave phenomenon: an observer attempts to see a wave function in flux but is presented instead with a particle; because we are viewing it, it changes. The arrow points in two directions, not one. Mindfulness is a one-way trip, an open circuit. Nature works in polarity and circuitry. The three questions: Where on the rim am I? What is the echo? What is the third force? "The tool shows you the shape of your prison. The shock at 6 is the key you have to forge yourself."

Your three-figure I Ching reading: moving lines as the active figure, still lines as the passive figure, the resulting hexagram as what the reconciling force produces; the cast hexagram is the sum, not a separate card. Caveats on provenance: Gurdjieff drew the figure in Russia around 1916 and never gave a derivation beyond 1/7 and the Law of Three. Rodin's doubling mod 9 is a modern arithmetic pattern; the resemblance is real, the link is ours. The Tesla "3, 6, 9" quote is almost certainly apocryphal. The personality Enneagram is a later attribution and deliberately set aside.

The 1 to 9 walk is symmetric under a half-turn around 5; 1-4-7 and 3-6-9 are complementary triangles pinned to the 2-5-8 axle. The Gardener-Warrior nine-year mapping as settled that day: Water at 1 and 2 (supply plus cultivation), Wall struck at 3, River at 4 (boundary from above), the reset at 5, Wall built at 6 (force plus boundary by choice), Mountain standing at 7 (force plus cultivation), Mountain still at 8, Ocean at 9 (the King, no function, pure sight).

The farm parable, the version you asked to read rather than hear. A woman took over her father's farm the winter he died. Wheat came in every autumn; the question was what the place would become. Year one she changed nothing, worked every job the way he had, and the farm filled her: his rhythm, the neighbors' habits, where each field held water. Year two she picked one thing to build: on the useless east slope she planted apple trees that wouldn't bear for most of a decade, and tended them every evening, and told no one why. Year three a spring storm took the roof off the barn; she stood in it and held, and the open roof showed her what it had hidden: the whole yard drained west, into the wheat, away from the apples. Year four the creek rose and cut through the west field, carrying off a season of topsoil; her brother drove over to dam it; she stopped him and let the water finish. Year five she sat on the barn floor with one question, what is this farm for, and didn't rebuild and didn't plant. Year six, the field bare and every row visible, she ploughed under half the wheat: one day, one decision, no going back; the farm had an edge now, grain west, trees east. Year seven the apples bore; nobody brought them in; she walked out and picked from trees she'd planted on bad ground five years before. Year eight the old west field gave out, as the drainage had promised; she let it lie fallow and kept what the orchard had raised. Year nine she walked down to where the creek met the sea and watched the sun lift the water that had carried off her soil, and saw what the question in the barn had been about: her father's farm had become hers, not because of the apples, but because she could now see the whole place at once. The next spring something new came to her, a seed she hadn't asked for. She didn't plan it yet. She took it in.

entries.s: Jung and the I Ching method
entries.t: The bend is enantiodromia, Jung's term for the way an extreme one-sidedness turns into its opposite. The method's warning that an unshocked process curves back toward the opposite of its origin is the same law, and the cause is the same: a system running on one force. The reconciling force is the transcendent function: holding two opposites in consciousness without collapsing into either until a third thing appears that was in neither, "of a different kind from both," the method's exact phrase. Pushing harder or giving up are each a refusal to hold the tension. Standstill is the tension held badly, as deadlock instead of as container.

entries.s: Jung and the I Ching method
entries.t: The shock has to come from outside the wiring; the shadow is what's outside the ego's wiring. The hexagon is the complex: autonomous, self-sufficient, recycling its own residue at the same level. That's repetition compulsion drawn as geometry. The method says the system cannot start itself; Jung says the impulse comes from the Self, which the ego experiences as other. 9 in the method, the Self in Jung. And the shadow is the first thing you meet on the way there. The third force very often turns out to be the thing the ego has been calling weakness. Echo pairs are the return of the repressed: nothing unfinished disappears; it reappears in a different place with a different face, and the line readings are what it will look like when it comes back. Differentiation is individuation's basic move: withdrawing projection, separating what is mine from what is hers. Insight into the shadow is not integration. Integration is when it's acted on and the self-image changes to include it. That's the same distinction the method makes between the lesson of a missed 6 and the shock itself.

If you expand the magic square from a three by three to a nine by nine, you can repeat the pattern and eventually you'll see all of them are on a diagonal. 714, 258, 369 always repeat, and they're on a diagonal; in the three by three all you see is two on one side and one on the other, but extended, those are two different diagonals repeating on their own line, infinitely. It's simple math, the mod three thing; it looks like it's something meaningful, and in the system I guess it is. The Lo Shu is quite literally a yin-yang symbol, squared and in cells and as numbers. You can take it as far as to say nine and one are the seeds of the other, the complementary side, the black with the white dot. I've always considered Kan and Li as straddling the line between yin and yang: fire is all yang but only as good as the substance it has to burn from, so it's pretty yin in nature; water fits the container of anything on the surface but will wear down any substance on earth, you can't break water, so it's almost the most yang thing. The 1/7 wiring gives the harmonic pattern. The law of seven is tied to Saturn through the magic squares of the planets.

Earth is the only family that's a straight line, and it's the mirror axis: reflect across 2-5-8 and the yin family lands on the yang family, 1 on 3, 4 on 6, 7 on 9. Reflect across the other diagonal and each family maps onto itself. The three families sum to 3, 6, 9 mod 9: the Law of Three isn't painted on top of the square, it's in the hexad's own material, and earth, with 5 at the center, is the hinge the reconciling force moves through. The Lo Shu is Saturn's own square, the 3 by 3 kamea, with 5 at its center.

Watts would call the inner process the Watercourse Way: water never forces, goes with the grain, around what it can't move, always toward the sea. His li, 理, is the organic pattern, the veins in jade, the grain in wood; it is a different character from the trigram Li, 離, fire, and reads as fire on any page with trigrams on it. His "mutual arising" translates 相生, xiang sheng, which is the Wu Xing generative cycle's own name, and five of the hexad's six links run with it; the sixth, 4 → 2, is wood breaking earth, the one controlling link, which is why the hexad can't be named for pure generation. Watercourse and Weather were rejected as names; the li and qi split stayed as the kinds: the hexad is the pattern, the triangle is the energy, and Ki is qi.

Rules of language that came out of corrections, in the order they were made: no solfège, points are numbers; "what are you holding" is new-agey and out, Jungian and Ki-nature metaphors only; no "charge," "deposit," or "return"; "compulsive" was a mishearing of "impulsive"; "the hub," "the well," "the depths," "Hoarfrost," "Calm," "Discernment," "Heaven," "Thunder" all replaced; "echo pair" retired for "interval trace"; "feeds" and "fed by" replaced by "trace"; "alone" dropped from the function lines; "gloss" rejected as a word, a second name is interchangeable with its figure; "given shock" and "made shock" retired; the Balanced is the label for every integrated pole; headlines are one capitalised word naming the point's place in the system, not its trigram.
